question: What are the biochemical analytical tools to assess the integrity and stability of LNPs?

ingredients.name: answer_critical_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer identifies reversed phase–ion pair HPLC (RP-IP HPLC), capillary electrophoresis (CE), and/or agarose/polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis as accepted methods to assess the integrity of encapsulated mRNA/nucleic acids in LNPs.
examples: RP-IP HPLC is a well-accepted method to assess mRNA integrity
Agarose or polyacrylamide gel or capillary electrophoresis (CE) can evaluate mRNA integrity
Nucleic acid integrity can be checked after extraction from LNPs using CE

ingredients.name: answer_critical_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer names cryogenic transmission electron microscopy (cryo-TEM) as the tool to visualize LNP morphology and core structure, including electron-dense cores in mRNA-LNPs and empty versus nucleic-acid-loaded LNPs, optionally mentioning thionine contrast enhancement.
examples: Cryo-TEM demonstrated the core structure of both unloaded and siRNA-containing LNPs
mRNA-LNPs show electron dense cores as revealed by cryo-TEM
Thionine was used for cryo-TEM contrast enhancement

ingredients.name: answer_critical_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer identifies dynamic light scattering (DLS) as the method to measure z-average diameter and polydispersity index over storage conditions, interpreting changes as aggregation or loss of LNP integrity (e.g., no size change at −80°C/4°C indicating maintained integrity; size growth at elevated temperatures indicating instability).
examples: DLS was used to characterize particle size and polydispersity
Frozen LNPs at −80°C showed no particle size change over time; lyophilized LNPs at 4°C maintained size integrity for at least 24 weeks
Particle-size increase reached a plateau after 4-week storage at 42°C while PDI remained <0.10

ingredients.name: answer_critical_3
ingredients.criterion: The answer explains that RP-IP HPLC separates mRNA via hydrophobic interactions with the stationary phase, using alkylammonium ion-pair salts and high salt to neutralize the polar phosphodiester backbone, enabling high-resolution, size-based separation.
examples: Alkylammonium salts increase hydrophobic interactions, driving selectivity based on sequence length
High salt concentrations neutralize the negative charge of the mRNA backbone
Separation is driven by hydrophobic interactions between analyte and stationary phase

ingredients.name: valuable_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer notes that CE separation is driven by size and charge, whereas RP-IP HPLC additionally retains selectivity to variations in mRNA hydrophobicity arising from sequence or chemical modifications.
examples: CE is driven by size and charge
Based on the ion pair system used, RP-IP retains selectivity to variations in mRNA hydrophobicity

ingredients.name: valuable_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer uses the structural distinction of LNPs from liposomes (lipids and some water in the core) to justify why both particle and cargo integrity must be assessed, since encapsulated mRNA can be exposed to an aqueous environment.
examples: A key aspect distinguishing LNPs from liposomes is the presence of lipids in the core
Data indicate water is present in the core, so mRNA could be exposed to an aqueous environment even when encapsulated

ingredients.name: valuable_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer states that assessing LNP integrity matters because it heavily impacts the potency and efficacy of the encapsulated nucleic acid therapeutic.
examples: LNP integrity heavily impacts the potency and efficacy of the encapsulated nucleic acids
LNPs are a promising platform for nucleic acid delivery to target tissues
